description: We are five CS students building the Lunar Landing Site Navigator around one question: will a lander survive where it touches down? Our project combines a battery Survival Mode simulation, landing uncertainty probabilities, and a 3D radio link beam. Our skills span AI/ML, computer vision, 3D graphics, backend, and dashboards, and we won first place at Smart City Hackathon Lahore. We seek help with orbital mechanics, lunar datasets (LRO, LOLA), and Python simulation.
summary:
GERTY is an interactive web platform that helps mission planners decide where to land near the lunar south pole. It integrates NASA data, including JPL Horizons ephemerides, LRO LOLA terrain and illumination maps, and LEND ice references, to score candidate sites on sunlight, slope, and proximity to ice.
For each site, GERTY renders a terrain-corrected 360° horizon showing when the Sun and Earth are visible, a 30 day timeline that separates power windows from communication blackouts, and a side by side site comparison. Users can also evaluate custom coordinates, and an AI Mission Advisor answers questions on terrain, visibility, and safety. Survival Mode extends this by simulating battery endurance, expressing landing uncertainty as a probability, and visualising the Earth radio link as a 3D beam.
This directly addresses the challenge of identifying safe, viable landing sites. It matters because the south pole holds water ice vital to future Artemis missions, yet its low sun angles and long shadows make a poor choice of site costly. GERTY turns scattered datasets into one clear decision tool.
details:
GERTY

“Dear Earth, we’ve found somewhere to land.”

At the Moon’s south pole, a crater rim can block sunlight or hide Earth even when it is above a flat horizon. That matters for solar power and direct-to-Earth communication. We built GERTY for the NASA Space Apps Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge to help users compare where and when those conditions overlap.

Users can choose from five preset sites, including Apollo 11 as a historical reference, or evaluate custom coordinates within the available map coverage. GERTY combines hourly Sun and Earth positions from NASA JPL Horizons with a 360° terrain profile calculated from NASA LOLA elevation data. It checks whether each body clears the terrain in its direction, then shows the results in an interactive Horizon View, a 30-day Timeline, and a side-by-side Compare view. Users can inspect candidate visibility windows in UTC, see how far the Sun and Earth clear the terrain, and ask the GERTY Adviser to explain the results.

Our design puts the view from the lunar surface at the center of the experience. The same hour stays in sync across views, so users can see how a nearby ridge affects the timeline and the comparison. We built GERTY with Next.js, TypeScript, React, Three.js, HTML Canvas, Python, Rasterio, Supabase, and Vercel. GERTY is a screening and education prototype. Mission decisions require finer terrain analysis, verified site measurements, and engineering checks for power, communications, and landing safety.

https://gerty-psi.vercel.app/

NASA LRO Lunar Exploration Neutron Detector (LEND) Data
